questions.q: What real analogy did the instructor use to explain what a struct is?
options: A paper form at the doctor's office, grouping name, age, address, and phone number together
questions.explain: The paper-form analogy captures it exactly: all those fields belong together and describe one person — just like a struct groups related fields into one unit.

questions.q: In `person1 = Person("Alice", 30, msg.sender);`, what does calling `getName()` return afterward?
options: Nothing — structs can't be read after being set
questions.explain: getName() returns person1.name, which was just set to "Alice" — confirmed live in the demo.

questions.q: What real guarantee does `mapping(address => Person) public directory;` combined with `msg.sender` as the key provide?
options: Only the contract's original deployer can ever call addPerson
All accounts share one single Person record
Each account automatically gets its own separate record that only it can read or overwrite via that key
It guarantees the struct can never be read back
questions.explain: Using msg.sender as the mapping key means every calling account is automatically keyed to its own record, separate from everyone else's.

questions.q: In the live demo, what happened when two different accounts each called addPerson with different data?
options: Both accounts ended up sharing identical data
Each account's data was stored separately, and getMyInfo() returned only that account's own record
The second call overwrote the first account's data entirely
Only the first account's call was ever accepted
questions.explain: One account stored "Carol", 56 and a different account stored "Alice", 57 — each account's getMyInfo() call returned only its own separately stored data.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe the struct-inside-a-mapping pattern as foundational for token standards?
options: Token standards never use structs or mappings
It has no real connection to tokens at all
It's the same real shape used later for tracking things like NFT metadata or a staking position per account
It's only useful for storing text messages
questions.explain: One struct describing a record, stored per-address in a mapping, is exactly the pattern more advanced token features (like per-account NFT metadata or staking) build on.
